title: What xtpd is
summary: Every XTP node runs exactly one multi-threaded network service daemon, xtpd. It takes registrations, service requests and network infrastructure peerages, and runs the matching hooks. Applications never handle a carrier socket, key, route or firewall rule. It is also where the node decides what survives damage. Design doc: https://claude.ai/artifact/5xdnepoEfSABaQoCxcByNe Built so far: xtpd dev1, packages/oorexx_xtpd_v0.1-dev1 (bin/xtpd.rex, src/Xtpd.cls; tests/run_all.sh). Next: the bootstrap role file (rexxos-grid-plan item 1), integrated into xtpd by its author, Claude (Opus 5.5).
authority: design (architecture Tom Dyer; written by Claude (Opus 5.5), 2026-11-24)
invariants: One xtpd per node; it is the node's only network process
Applications are hooks; they never hold a carrier socket, key, route or firewall rule
Nothing in this sphere is built or field-tested
procedure: Read xtpd.addressing before designing any XTP client or service
Read xtpd.decisions for what Tom has not yet decided

provenance.claim: XTP sessions: one context, both directions, per-direction close, one listener socket for all sessions
Service name to class to logical peer to route; IP addresses only in the route table; admission before CNTL

qualification_boundaries.status: dev1 built: packages/oorexx_xtpd_v0.1-dev1 (Claude (Opus 5.5), 24 Nov 2026) - registrations, peerages and keys from files, unix-socket OPEN with descriptor passing, exec hooks, the fence, receipts through oorexx_logging
qualification_boundaries.field: tested on loopback only (two daemons, real OpenSSH over UDP and raw IP 36); not field-tested; LDAP inputs, operating states, emergency files and the role bootstrap are not built
